title: EFFECTS OF COLOR TEMPERATURE ON PROJECTED FRACTAL LIGHT PATTERNS: VISUAL INTEREST AND EMOTIONAL RESPONSE

findings.antecedent: two-dimensional fractal pattern complexity D = 1.7
findings.mechanism: Fractal fluency theory suggests mid-complexity is preferred, but higher complexity (D=1.7) was found most interesting in this study, possibly due to the range of patterns presented.
findings.quote: visual interest rating was the highest for high-complexity fractal pattern D = 1.7, (Mean: 10.57, SD: 3.8).

findings.antecedent: two-dimensional fractal pattern complexity (D value) from 1.1 to 1.7
findings.mechanism: Visual interest increased with complexity up to a certain point (D=1.7), then decreased.
findings.quote: as D value increased from D = 1.1 to D = 1.7, visual interest increased gradually, after which visual interest dropped for D = 1.9 (Mean: 8, SD: 5.9).

findings.antecedent: two-dimensional fractal pattern complexity D = 1.1
findings.mechanism: Low complexity fractal patterns were found least visually interesting.
findings.quote: fractal pattern of D = 1.1 (Mean: 4.13, SD: 4.9) was the least visually interesting among all the fractal patterns

findings.antecedent: two-dimensional fractal pattern complexity D = 1.7 vs D = 1.5
findings.quote: Results also demonstrated no significant difference between visual interest of fractal patterns for D = 1.7 and D = 1.5.

findings.antecedent: different two-dimensional fractal pattern complexity levels
findings.mechanism: Wilcoxon Signed-rank test showed significant differences for most pairs, indicating complexity generally influences visual interest.
findings.quote: Wilcoxon Signed-rank test results demonstrated a significant difference on visual interest ratings among most of the fractal patterns complexity levels.

findings.antecedent: two-dimensional fractal pattern complexity D = 1.3 vs D = 1.9
findings.mechanism: Both D=1.3 (too simple) and D=1.9 (too complex) were among the least preferred, leading to no significant difference between them.
findings.quote: fractal pattern complexity levels did not demonstrate a significant difference in terms of visual interest ratings; D = 1.3 and D = 1.9

findings.antecedent: two-dimensional fractal pattern complexity D = 1.5 vs D = 1.9
findings.quote: fractal pattern complexity levels did not demonstrate a significant difference in terms of visual interest ratings; D = 1.5 and D = 1.9

findings.antecedent: two-dimensional fractal pattern complexity levels
findings.mechanism: Participants generally rated pleasure items as 'neutral' across all complexity levels.
findings.quote: the complexity of fractal patterns had no significant influence on participants’ pleasure state

findings.antecedent: two-dimensional fractal pattern complexity levels
findings.mechanism: Increasing complexity levels induced increased arousal states, with D=1.9 showing the highest 'wide-awake' response and D=1.1 the lowest 'sluggish' response.
findings.quote: it had a significant positive influence on participants’ arousal state.

findings.antecedent: two-dimensional fractal pattern complexity D = 1.1 vs D = 1.9
findings.mechanism: A significant difference was observed between the lowest and highest complexity levels for pleasure.
findings.quote: there was a significant difference between the effect of complexity levels on participants’ pleasure state for the levels D = 1.1 and D = 1.9

findings.antecedent: two-dimensional fractal pattern complexity levels (excluding D=1.1 vs D=1.9)
